target_customer: Brands, agencies and media buyers purchasing online video advertising
problem: Online video ads were passive and hard to measure for engagement. 140Fire let advertisers layer interactive polls and questions over video ads and collect response data.
business_model: Video ad network taking a margin on media buys, with an overlay and data product (DataRoll)

founders.name: Jason Wilk
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists only Jason Wilk and gives no background. Background not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Paras Chitakar
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch coverage of the February 2011 launch, which says the company was started in January 2010. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Tremor Media
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as an established player in video advertising

competitors.name: ScanScout
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as an established player

competitors.name: Kit Digital
competitors.what: Video advertising and delivery company (named as Kit)
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as an established player

technical_complexity.rationale: Overlay editor, ad server integration and real-time result aggregation at scale. TechCrunch says the backend reused Flektor technology from team members who built that product, which lowered the build effort.

defensibility.rationale: Interactive overlays could be copied by larger video ad networks. The edge was the early editor and ad-server integration plus publisher relationships, not structural.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established video ad networks were already consolidating in 2010 and 2011. The company was sold in 2015, but the buyer was not found in opened sources.

market_need_then: Online video ad spend was growing in 2010 and 2011 and advertisers wanted engagement and response data beyond view counts. The sources show launch coverage but no spend figures.

rebrands.why: Not sourced. YC lists the company as All Screen with the 140Fire description, and Wikipedia calls the sold business AllScreen.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand search found no press about the name, mascot or community. Only B2B launch coverage mentions Mark Cuban as a backer, which was a credibility signal rather than a brand asset.

outcome_analysis: 140Fire launched in February 2011 with Mark Cuban and the Kraft family as backers and sold an interactive overlay on video ads inside an ad network. Wikipedia says founder Jason Wilk sold a video ad business called AllScreen for about 85 million dollars in 2015, which funded Dave. The buyer and the exact link between 140Fire and AllScreen are not confirmed in opened sources, so the exit value is left null.
notes: Company website 140fire.com returned HTTP 520 on fetch, treated as dead or unavailable. Wikipedia and a Dealroom profile give an 85 million dollar sale in 2015, but neither names the buyer; recorded as unverified and kept out of exit amount. No funding amounts found anywhere. Success factor distribution_advantage is weakly supported; Mark Cuban backing is the only evidence.
